## Spotify ads team: call brief

**Who they are.** Spotify is a music, podcast and audiobook platform. Its advertising business sells [audio, video, display and carousel ads](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/ad-formats/) to brands and agencies. In Q3 2026, Spotify reported [788 million monthly active users, 306 million Premium subscribers and €5.0 billion in quarterly revenue](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2026-10-22/spotify-q3-2026-earnings/).

**What changed recently.**
- **Oct. 22:** Spotify reported 11% year-over-year user growth and said its creator Partner Program was expanding to [more than 35 new markets](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2026-10-22/spotify-q3-2026-earnings/).
- **Oct. 20:** It began rolling out [podcast Memberships in 34 markets](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2026-10-20/spotify-memberships-creators/). Creators can offer perks including fewer ads, alongside other monetization options.

**Who you’re meeting.** You haven’t named the attendees. Share their names and I can add a line on each.

**Three things to lead with or ask**
1. **Proving performance:** “What would a controlled test look like, and how would you measure incremental outcomes?” Spotify’s [performance playbook](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/news-and-insights/ads-manager-performance-playbook/) emphasizes measurement, bidding and format strategy.
2. **Audio plus video:** “For our objective and budget, when does adding video or display to audio justify the extra spend?” Spotify promotes [multi-format campaigns](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/ad-formats/).
3. **Retail measurement, if relevant:** “Can we use retailer audiences and connect exposure to sales?” Spotify describes a [Walmart DSP integration](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/news-and-insights/spotify-ad-exchange-walmart-dsp/) for U.S. advertisers with closed-loop measurement.
